items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] are discrete random variables, where the conditional expected value of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] is given by [MATH: \mu_{X|y}.] In other words,

Content:
[MATH: \textrm{E}[X\,|\,Y=y] = \mu_{X|y}.]

Content:
The conditional variance of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] is defined as

Content:
[MATH: \textrm{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] = \textrm{E}\big[(X - \mu_{X|y} \big)^2 \,|\, Y=y].]

Content:
This is similar to the definition of [MATH: \textrm{Var}[X]] in that it represents the average (squared) distance of the random variable [MATH: X] from the mean. The difference here is that the expected values are now dependent on the outcome of [MATH: Y.]

Content:
Similarly to the case of [MATH: \textrm{Var}[X],] this often isn't the easiest formula to use in practice. However, it can be shown that the definition of conditional variance is equivalent to

Content:
[MATH: Var[X|Y = y]|= E[X^{2}|Y = y] − μ_{X|y}^{2}; = [∑_(x)x^{2}f_{X|Y}(x|y)] − μ_{X|y}^{2},]

Content:
where [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y)] is the conditional PMF of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y.] Note that these formulas are analogous to those for [MATH: \textrm{Var}[X].]

Content:
Finally, we have an analogous definition for the conditional variance of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: Var[Y|X = x]|= E[(Y − μ_{Y|x})^{2}|X = x]; = E[Y^{2}|X = x] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}; = [∑_(y)y^{2}f_{Y|X}(y|x)] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}]

Recall that the conditional variance of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x] is defined by

[MATH: Var[Y|X = x]|= E[(Y − μ_{Y|x})^{2}|X = x]; = E[Y^{2}|X = x] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}; = [∑_(y)y^{2}f_{Y|X}(y|x)] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}.]

Therefore, we obtain [MATH: Var[Y|X = 3]|= [∑_(y)y^{2}f_{Y|X}(y|3)] − μ_{Y|3}^{2}; = [(1)^{2} ⋅ (1)/(3) + (2)^{2} ⋅ (1)/(6) + (4)^{2} ⋅ (1)/(2)] − ((8)/(3))^{2}; = (1)/(3) + (2)/(3) + 8 − (64)/(9); = (17)/(9).]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that [MATH: X] and [MATH: Y] are discrete random variables, where the conditional expected value of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] is given by [MATH: \mu_{X|y}.] In other words,

Content:
[MATH: \textrm{E}[X\,|\,Y=y] = \mu_{X|y}.]

Content:
The conditional variance of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y=y] is defined as

Content:
[MATH: \textrm{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] = \textrm{E}\big[(X - \mu_{X|y} \big)^2 \,|\, Y=y].]

Content:
This is similar to the definition of [MATH: \textrm{Var}[X]] in that it represents the average (squared) distance of the random variable [MATH: X] from the mean. The difference here is that the expected values are now dependent on the outcome of [MATH: Y.]

Content:
Similarly to the case of [MATH: \textrm{Var}[X],] this often isn't the easiest formula to use in practice. However, it can be shown that the definition of conditional variance is equivalent to

Content:
[MATH: Var[X|Y = y]|= E[X^{2}|Y = y] − μ_{X|y}^{2}; = [∑_(x)x^{2}f_{X|Y}(x|y)] − μ_{X|y}^{2},]

Content:
where [MATH: f_{X|Y}(x \,|\, y)] is the conditional PMF of [MATH: X] given [MATH: Y.] Note that these formulas are analogous to those for [MATH: \textrm{Var}[X].]

Content:
Finally, we have an analogous definition for the conditional variance of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: Var[Y|X = x]|= E[(Y − μ_{Y|x})^{2}|X = x]; = E[Y^{2}|X = x] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}; = [∑_(y)y^{2}f_{Y|X}(y|x)] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}]

---

Find [MATH: \textrm{Var}\big[Y \,|\, X=3\big]] given that the conditional probability mass function [MATH: f_{Y|X}(y \,|\, 3)] is shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is [MATH: \mu_{Y|3} = \dfrac{8}{3}.]

Explanation:
Recall that the conditional variance of [MATH: Y] given [MATH: X=x] is defined by

[MATH: Var[Y|X = x]|= E[(Y − μ_{Y|x})^{2}|X = x]; = E[Y^{2}|X = x] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}; = [∑_(y)y^{2}f_{Y|X}(y|x)] − μ_{Y|x}^{2}.]

Therefore, we obtain
[MATH: Var[Y|X = 3]|= [∑_(y)y^{2}f_{Y|X}(y|3)] − μ_{Y|3}^{2}; = [(1)^{2} ⋅ (1)/(3) + (2)^{2} ⋅ (1)/(6) + (4)^{2} ⋅ (1)/(2)] − ((8)/(3))^{2}; = (1)/(3) + (2)/(3) + 8 − (64)/(9); = (17)/(9).]
